docs.text: BER Format Check Dialog Guide The BER format check dialog checks whether BER-encoded data matches a supported PKI format. It can identify a format, validate a selected format, open format-specific details, or decode the data in the main BerEditor window. Open it from Tool > Check BER . Figure 1. BER format check dialog. Provide a file or encoded source, identify or select a format, then choose the appropriate check or view action. Supported Formats The dialog can identify or check these formats: Certificate CRL (certificate revocation list) CSR (certificate signing request) PublicKey PrivateKey PrivateKeyInfo EncPrivateKey (encrypted private key) CMS PKCS7 OCSP response CMP message Screen Areas Format list — Shows the formats supported by the checker. BER file — Select this to use a file as the source. The Find button opens a BER file picker, and the path is shown beside the checkbox. Source format — When BER file is unchecked, choose how the source text is represented: Hex or Base64 . Source length — Shows the calculated length for the selected source representation. Source input — Enter or paste the encoded bytes when using text input. BER Type Check — Detects the source's supported PKI format and selects it in the format list. Format selector — Choose a specific format to validate or inspect. Format Check — Checks whether the source conforms to the selected format and reports success or an error. V — Opens the format-specific information view after validating the selected format. Encrypted private keys require a password. D — Decodes the source in the main BerEditor window using the selected format title. Clear — Clears the file path and source text. Close — Closes the dialog. Check a Source File or Value Choose the source method: To check a file, select BER file , then select Find and choose the file. To check encoded text, leave BER file unchecked, select Hex or Base64 , and enter the source in the input area. Select BER Type Check to detect a supported format, or choose the expected format from the format selector. Select Format Check to validate the source against the selected format. Read the success message or the reported format error. Open Details or Decode After choosing a format, select V to open its detail window. The selected format must pass its format check. Available detail views include certificate, CRL, CSR, public/private key, CMS/PKCS7, OCSP response, and CMP message information. Select D to decode the source in the main BER view. A format must be selected first. For an encrypted private key, V prompts for the password before showing key details. Notes and Troubleshooting When using text input, the source must match its selected representation ( Hex or Base64 ). Invalid or empty input cannot be checked. BER Type Check identifies only the formats listed above. If the source is unsupported or malformed, the dialog reports that it could not determine a supported format. Format Check requires a format selection. Choose the expected type or run BER Type Check first. Use Clear before starting a new check to remove the previous file path and source text.
docs.title: Check BER

docs.text: BER Compare Dialog Guide The BER Compare dialog compares two BER files by their encoded bytes and decoded tree structure. Open it from Tool > BER Compare . Figure 1. BER Compare dialog. Load one file into each side, then compare the structures and inspect matched values. Screen Areas SET order support — Enables matching of SET children without relying on their position in the tree. Use this when the order of SET elements should not affect matching. A File / B File — Shows the selected file path for each side. Find — Selects a BER file for side A or B and loads its decoded tree. D — Decodes the corresponding file in BerEditor's main window. A BER Information / B BER Information — Displays the decoded BER tree for each file. Selecting a node highlights it and its corresponding node on the other side when a match is found. BER A and B value — Shows the selected nodes' headers and values side by side. If hidden, select Show Value to display this pane. Status / Compare — Select Compare to compare the loaded BER data. The status reports whether A and B are the same or different. Clear — Clears both file paths, trees, and value panes. Show Value — Shows the BER A and B value pane. Close — Closes the dialog. Compare Two BER Files Select Find on the A File row and choose the first BER file. Select Find on the B File row and choose the second BER file. Optionally enable SET order support if SET elements may appear in a different order. Select Compare . Read the status message. Matching tree nodes are highlighted; select a node to inspect its corresponding node and value on the other side. You can also drag and drop two local files onto the dialog. The first file fills A and the second fills B. If both sides are already populated, clear the dialog before dropping different files. Inspect or Decode a File Select a node in either tree to display its encoded header and value in the comparison pane. Select D beside a file path to decode that file in the main BerEditor window. If the value pane is not visible, select Show Value . Select Clear before starting another comparison. How Results Are Determined The dialog first checks whether the complete BER byte sequences are identical. For differing files, it compares nodes by tag, tree depth, definite/indefinite length form, length, and value. A difference in any of these makes the corresponding nodes different. With SET order support enabled, SET children are matched by their parent path rather than their original position. Both files must be loaded before comparison. If either side is empty, BerEditor asks you to select that file.
docs.title: BER Compare Dialog Guide

docs.text: Binary View Dialog Guide The Binary View dialog displays binary data as Base64, a formatted hexadecimal dump, or a continuous hexadecimal value. Open it from Tool > Binary View . Figure 1. Binary View dialog. Base64 is selected by default; use Find to load a file and change the output format as needed. The implementation file is named bin_view_dlg , while the menu and dialog call this feature Binary View . Screen Areas Find — Opens a file picker and loads a binary file for viewing. Base64 — Displays the data as Base64 text. This is the default format. Hex — Displays a hexadecimal dump in rows of up to 16 bytes. Raw — Displays the complete hexadecimal value without row formatting. Address — In Hex view, includes each row's offset. Available only in Hex view. ASCII — In Hex view, adds printable characters beside each row. Available only in Hex view. PEM — Wraps Base64 output with BEGIN and END lines. Available only in Base64 view. PEM type — Selects or enters the label used in the PEM header and footer. The list includes common key, certificate, CSR, CRL, PKCS#7/CMS, and parameter labels. Output area — Shows the selected representation. It is read-only. Print / Print Preview — Prints the displayed output or previews it before printing. Close — Closes the dialog. View Binary Data Select Find and choose a file, or open Binary View from a selected value in BerEditor. Choose Base64 , Hex , or Raw . For Hex view, optionally enable Address and ASCII . For Base64 view, optionally enable PEM and choose or enter a PEM type. Use Print or Print Preview if you need a paper copy. Display updates automatically when the format or its options change. The data area is read-only. A local file can also be dragged onto the dialog to load it. Format Details Base64 output is line-wrapped. With PEM enabled, the selected label is used in the PEM boundary lines. Hex output is grouped into 16-byte rows. Address shows the offset, and ASCII shows printable characters for each row. Raw output is a continuous hexadecimal string; Address and ASCII options are unavailable.
docs.title: Binary View

docs.text: Get BER from URI Dialog Guide The Get BER from URI dialog retrieves BER-encoded data from an HTTP(S) or LDAP address and loads the result into the main BerEditor window for decoding. Open it from Tool > Get BER from URI . Figure 1. Get BER from URI dialog. Enter an HTTP(S) or LDAP address, or enable LDAP Host Information to supply LDAP connection and search details separately. Screen Areas URI Address — Enter or select an address. Recent addresses are available from the drop-down list. The dialog accepts http , https , and ldap schemes. Example — Shows an example certificate URL. Clear Used URI — Removes the saved recent URI list. Use LDAP Host Information — Switches from a full URI to separately entered LDAP connection details. When enabled, the URI field is disabled and the LDAP Host Information group is enabled. LDAP Host Information — Enter the LDAP server Host , Port , and search DN . The host and port are retained as settings for later use. LDAP Search Condition — Supplies LDAP search options: Scope , certificate Type , and Filter . The default filter is (objectClass=*) . Get — Retrieves data from the selected address and asks BerEditor to decode the returned data. Close — Closes the dialog. Retrieve Data from an HTTP(S) URI Leave Use LDAP Host Information unchecked. Enter or select an http:// or https:// address in URI Address . Select Get . If retrieval succeeds, BerEditor decodes the returned data in the main window and displays a success message. The address can also be selected from the recent URI list. Successfully used addresses are saved in that list. Clear Used URI removes the saved list. Retrieve Data from LDAP You can provide LDAP details in either of these ways: Use an LDAP URI Leave Use LDAP Host Information unchecked. Enter an ldap:// URI that identifies the LDAP server and search location. Set the search Type and Filter if needed. Select Get . The dialog reads the server, DN, scope, filter, and requested attribute from the LDAP URI when those values are present. The selected Type and filter field are used as defaults where the URI does not specify them. Enter LDAP Host Information Separately Select Use LDAP Host Information . Enter the LDAP server Host , Port , and DN . Choose a Scope , Type , and Filter . Select Get . The current implementation provides the BASE scope. Available certificate types are caCertificate , signCertificate , userCertificate , certificateRevocationList , autorithRevocationList , deltaRevocationList , and certificateTrustList . Troubleshooting Enter an address before selecting Get . The dialog reports an error when the URI is empty or uses an unsupported scheme. For LDAP host mode, provide a DN. Check the host, port, and server availability if connection or bind errors appear. If retrieval fails, BerEditor reports the retrieval error in a warning or log message. Retrieved data is passed to the main BER decoder. If the server returns data that is not valid BER, decoding may fail even when the network request succeeds.
docs.title: Get BER from URI

docs.text: Make BER Dialog Guide The Make BER dialog builds a BER-encoded value from a tag and value. Open it from Tool > Make BER . Figure 1. Make BER dialog. The header and BER output are updated as the tag settings and value change. Screen Areas More Type — Adds additional universal tag types to the Tag type list. Class — Selects the BER tag class: Universal , Application , Content-Specific , or Private . Constructed — Sets the constructed bit. SEQUENCE and SET are always constructed; other universal types cannot be changed to constructed in this dialog. Indefinite — Uses indefinite length for constructed data. This option is enabled only when Constructed is selected. The generated BER ends with the end-of-contents marker 00 00 . Tag / Number — For the Universal class, select a tag type from the list. For the other classes, enter the tag number in hexadecimal. The tag number for Content-Specific is limited to 1F (31) or less in this dialog. Tag bits — Shows the BER tag byte in binary ( [T] 0b ). L — Shows the generated length field in hexadecimal. Value format and input — Select the input representation and enter the value. Available formats are Hex , String , and Base64 . The Len field shows the decoded value length. C — Clears the value input. Make Value — Opens a helper for supported value types such as BitString, Integer, or ObjectIdentifier. Availability depends on the selected tag and value format. BER Header — Displays the generated tag and length bytes in hexadecimal. BER output — Displays the complete BER value in hexadecimal. Its Len field shows the output length. Make — Validates and accepts the generated BER value. From Tool > Make BER , the value is then loaded into the main BER view. Close — Closes the dialog without accepting the generated value. Create a BER Value Open Tool > Make BER . Choose a Class . For Universal , choose a tag type. Use More Type if the required universal type is not in the initial list. For another class, enter the tag Number in hexadecimal. Set Constructed or Indefinite if applicable. These controls are constrained by the selected tag class and type. Select the value format, then enter the value. The BER Header and BER output update as you edit the settings. Review the header, length, and complete BER output. Select Make to validate and load the result into the main BER view. Tag and Value Notes The default universal tag is SEQUENCE , with Constructed enabled. NULL has no value input; the value field is disabled for this tag. SEQUENCE and SET require the Constructed bit. Other universal tag types are treated as primitive by this dialog. For a constructed value with Indefinite selected, the BER output uses an indefinite length and appends 00 00 as the end-of-contents marker. A BER BOOLEAN value must be exactly one byte. For BIT STRING , the first value byte must be between 00 and 07 , representing the number of unused bits. For non-universal classes, enter the tag number in hexadecimal. The Content-Specific class uses a low tag number up to 1F here. If Validation Fails If the selected input format cannot be decoded, BerEditor reports a format error and returns focus to the value field. Correct the input format or value, then select Make again. Boolean and BitString values have the additional constraints listed above.

docs.text: Text View Dialog Guide The Text View dialog presents decoded BER or KMIP TTLV data as an indented text listing, or shows its hexadecimal values. Open it from Tool > Text View . Figure 1. Text View dialog. String View is selected by default; choose Hex View to inspect encoded bytes. Screen Areas Find — Loads a binary file to view. BerEditor parses it as BER or, when detected, KMIP TTLV. String View — Displays parsed fields and values in an indented text layout. This is the default view. Hex View — Displays parsed structures and their hexadecimal bytes. View Information — Adds an ASCII/printable-text column in Hex View. This option is available only in Hex View and is disabled for String View. Output area — Shows the listing. It is read-only and does not wrap long lines. Print / Print Preview — Prints the displayed listing or previews it before printing. Close — Closes the dialog. View Data Open Text View from the selected data in BerEditor, or select Find to load a file. Choose String View or Hex View . In Hex View, optionally select View Information to show printable characters alongside hexadecimal bytes. Scroll through the parsed output. Use Print or Print Preview if needed. The viewer detects KMIP TTLV data and displays its parsed structure. Otherwise, it parses the input as BER. You can also drag and drop a local file onto the dialog. View Modes String View focuses on decoded values and structure. The information-column option is unavailable in this mode. Hex View shows bytes in groups of up to 16, with offsets and structural indentation. Enable View Information to include printable text beside the bytes. The view area is read-only; use the main BerEditor tools to edit or construct data.
docs.title: Text View

docs.text: Data Converter Dialog Guide The Data Converter converts data between text and common encoded representations. Open it from Tool > Data Converter . Figure 1. Data Converter dialog layout. This is an illustrative diagram based on the UI definition, not a screenshot of the running application. Screen Areas Read File — Loads a file into the input area as hexadecimal data. Input format and input area — Choose the format of the source data and enter or paste its value. Input Len — Shows the length calculated using the selected input format. Conversion — Converts the source bytes to the selected output format. Conversion Format — Selects the output representation. Show printable text is available when String is selected. docs.text: Decode BER Dialog Guide The Decode BER dialog converts BER data entered as text into bytes and loads it into BerEditor for decoding. Open it from Tool > Decode BER . Figure 1. Decode BER dialog. The format controls and file picker are above the input area; Clear, Decode, and Close are along the bottom. Screen Areas Input format — Choose Hex , Base64 , or Base64URL . The selected option determines how BerEditor interprets the text in the input area. Find — Opens a file picker to load a BER file into the input area. Len — Shows the calculated data length for the current input and format. This field is read-only. Input area — Enter or paste the encoded data. Its placeholder indicates the selected format. Clear — Removes the text from the input area. Decode — Decodes the input and loads it into the main BerEditor window. Close — Closes the dialog. Dialog Controls Control Description Hex Treats the input as hexadecimal data. This is the default format. Base64 Treats the input as Base64 data. The input may also be a PEM value. Base64URL Treats the input as URL-safe Base64 data. Input area Enter or paste the encoded data here. The placeholder changes with the selected format. Len Displays the calculated data length for the current format. It is read-only. Find Selects a BER file and loads its contents into the input area using the selected format. Clear Clears the input area. Decode Decodes the entered data and loads it into the main BerEditor window. Close Closes the dialog. Decode Data Open Tool > Decode BER . Select the input format: Hex , Base64 , or Base64URL . Enter or paste the encoded data into the input area. Review the value shown in Len . Select Decode . When decoding succeeds, the dialog closes and BerEditor displays the decoded data in the main window. If the input area is empty, the application asks you to enter data. If the data cannot be parsed in the selected format, a format error is displayed. Load Data from a File Select the desired input format. Select Find and choose a BER file. The file contents are placed in the input area in the selected format. Select Decode to load the data into the main window. The file picker checks that the selected file can be read as BER data. If it is not a valid BER file, BerEditor displays an error. Drag and Drop You can drag a local file onto the dialog to load it into the input area. The dialog converts the file contents to the currently selected representation: hexadecimal, Base64, or Base64URL. Then select Decode to inspect the data. Tips Make sure the selected format matches the text you entered. For example, choose Base64URL for URL-safe Base64 text. Use Clear before entering a different value if you want to avoid mixing it with existing input. Len is calculated from the selected encoding; it is not an editable field. The dialog processes BER data. Other data formats may produce a decoding or format error.

docs.text: BerEditor Main Window UI Guide This guide describes the main BerEditor window based on src/BerEditor/mainwindow.cpp and src/BerEditor/mainwindow.h . Image note: The supplied file images/mainwindow.png currently shows the Data Converter dialog, not the BerEditor main window. It is included below as provided so the mismatch is visible. Replace it with a main-window capture when one is available. Figure 1. The supplied image currently shows the Data Converter dialog. The main-window layout described below is based on the application source code. Main Window Layout The main window is divided into a left BER tree pane and a right workspace. The right workspace has an upper data viewer and a lower information/log panel. Splitters let the user adjust the pane sizes. Area Description Menu bar Provides File, Edit, Tool, Cryptography, Service, Protocol, KMIP, Help, and View commands. Toolbars Optional toolbars provide shortcuts to commands from the menus. Which toolbars and buttons appear can be configured in View. BER tree (left) Displays the decoded BER structure as a navigable tree. Select a node to inspect its data and details. Data viewer (upper right) Shows the selected data in Hex , XML , Text , or JSON tabs. The Hex view is displayed as a table with an address, byte columns, and printable text. Information (lower right) Shows details about the currently selected node or data. Log (lower right) Shows application messages and operation output. Status bar Displays status information when an operation provides it. Some data-view tabs and the Log tab may be unavailable depending on license status. The exact presentation can also vary by platform and window size. Menus Menu Main purpose File Create a new window; open BER, certificate, CRL, CSR, key, or CMS data; save; view recent files; print; and quit. Edit Copy selected information as-is, Hex, or Base64; expand or collapse tree nodes; navigate between nodes; and find a node. Tool Decode BER; convert data or numbers; inspect OIDs; create or check BER; retrieve BER from a URI; compare BER; and open binary/text views. Cryptography Manage keys and perform hash, MAC, encryption, signature, key agreement, PKCS#7, secret sharing, certificate path validation, OTP, VID, and big-number operations. Service Manage key pairs, certificates, and keys; check SSL/TLS; compare X.509 certificates; sign documents; and access CAVP tools. PDF signing appears when enabled in the build. Protocol Open clients for OCSP, TSP, CMP, SCEP, ACME, and EST. KMIP Decode, create, encode, or send KMIP TTLV messages. Help Configure settings; clear or pause logging; open PKI content, license information, support links, and About information. View Configure which toolbar actions are shown and restore the default view configuration. For the full command list and shortcuts, see Menu Guide . Typical Workflow Use File > Open... to open a BER file, or choose the appropriate specialized open command for a certificate, CRL, CSR, key, or CMS file. Select a node in the BER tree on the left. Inspect the selected data in the Hex, XML, Text, or JSON viewer tabs on the right. Read node details in Information and operation messages in Log . Use File > Save or File > Save As... when you need to save the current BER data. Resizing and View Options Drag the divider between the tree and right workspace to change their relative widths. Drag the divider between the upper data viewer and lower Information/Log panel to change their heights. Use the View menu to show or hide toolbar actions and Set Default to restore the configured default view. If an expected action or data tab is unavailable, check the license status and the current View configuration.

docs.text: BerEditor Menu Guide This document describes the main menus created in mainwindow.cpp . Some items may be hidden or disabled depending on build options or license status. File Menu item Description New Opens a new BerEditor window. Open... Opens a BER file. Open Certificate Opens a certificate file. Open CRL Opens a certificate revocation list (CRL) file. Open CSR Opens a certificate signing request (CSR) file. Open PrivateKey Opens a private key file. Open PublicKey Opens a public key file. Open CMS Opens a CMS file. Save / Save As... Saves the current data or saves it under another name. Recent Files Reopens a recently used file. Up to 10 entries are maintained. Print / Print Preview Prints the current content or previews it before printing. Quit Exits BerEditor. Edit Menu item Description Copy Information Copies the contents of the current selection to the clipboard. Copy As Hex Copies the selected value in hexadecimal format. Copy As Base64 Copies the selected value in Base64 format. Expand All / Expand Node Expands all nodes in the BER tree or the selected node. Collapse All / Collapse Node Collapses all nodes in the BER tree or the selected node. Previous Node / Next Node Moves to the previous or next node in the tree. Find Searches for a node in the BER data. Tool Menu item Description Decode BER Decodes BER data. Data Converter Converts data character encodings or representations. Num Converter Converts numeric representations. OID Information Looks up Object Identifier (OID) information. Make BER Creates BER data. Check BER Checks the format and validity of BER data. Get BER from URI Retrieves BER data from a URI. BER Compare Compares two BER data values. Binary View / Text View Opens data in binary or text view. Cryptography Menu item Description Key Manage Provides key derivation and key encryption/decryption functions. Hash Generates a hash value. Message Authentication Code Generates a message authentication code (MAC). Encrypt/Decrypt Encrypts or decrypts data. Sign/Verify Creates or verifies a digital signature. PubKey Encrypt/Decrypt Encrypts or decrypts data using a public key. Key Agreement Performs DH or ECDH key agreement. PKCS7 Creates and validates PKCS#7 messages. Shamir Secret Sharing Splits a key or combines key shares. Certificate Path Validation Validates a certificate path. OTP Generator Generates a one-time password (OTP). VID Generates and validates VID values. BN Calculator Performs big number calculations. Make PrivateKey Generates a private key. Service Menu item Description KeyPair Manage Lists and manages asymmetric key pairs. Certificate Manage Lists and manages certificates and keys. Key List Lists and manages symmetric keys. SSL Check Checks SSL/TLS protocol connections. X509 Compare Compares X.509 information. Document Signer Provides document digital signing functions. PDF Signer Provides PDF digital signing functions. Availability depends on build options. CAVP Provides cryptographic algorithm validation functions. Protocol Menu item Description OCSP client Checks certificate status using OCSP. TSP client Processes Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP) requests. CMP client Processes Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) requests. SCEP client Processes SCEP certificate enrollment requests. ACME client Processes ACME protocol requests. EST client Processes EST protocol requests. KMIP Menu item Description Decode TTLV Decodes KMIP TTLV messages. Make TTLV Creates KMIP TTLV messages. TTLV Encoder Encodes TTLV messages. TTLV Client Runs the KMIP TTLV client. Help Menu item Description Settings Configures the application environment. Clear Log Clears messages in the Log tab. Log Pauses or resumes logging. Content Displays PKI-related information. License Information Displays license and registration information. Bug or Issue Report Reports bugs or issues. Q and A Opens question-and-answer information. About BerEditor Displays information about BerEditor. Menu Shortcuts Shortcut notation may vary by operating system. The following combinations are based on those assigned in the source code. Menu item Shortcut Open Ctrl+O Open Certificate / CRL / CSR F2 / F3 / F4 Save / Save As Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S Print Ctrl+P Copy Information Ctrl+C Copy As Hex / Base64 Ctrl+X / Ctrl+B Expand All / Expand Node F5 / F6 Collapse All / Collapse Node F7 / F8 Previous Node / Next Node Ctrl+← / Ctrl+→ Find Ctrl+F Clear Log / Log F9 / F10 Content / About BerEditor F11 / F1 Note: Menu names follow the English UI labels. Check the running application for the exact translations, platform-specific shortcuts, and availability under your license.

docs.text: Number Converter Dialog Guide The Number Converter converts a number between binary, decimal, and hexadecimal representations. Open it from Tool > Num Converter . Figure 1. Number Converter dialog. Enter a value at the top; the equivalent values appear in the three output sections below. Screen Areas Number Type — Select the radix of the value entered in the input field: Bit (base 2), Decimal (base 10), or Hex (base 16). Decimal is selected by default. Input field — Enter the value to convert. The placeholder indicates valid characters for the selected type. Input Clear — Clears the input field. Binary output — Shows the equivalent binary representation. Its length is shown in the small read-only field beside the up-arrow button. Decimal output — Shows the equivalent decimal representation and its length. Hex output — Shows the equivalent hexadecimal representation and its length. Up-arrow buttons — Copy that section's value to the input field and select its matching input type, allowing conversion from that representation. Output Clear — Clears all three converted values and their lengths. Close — Closes the dialog. Convert a Number Select the input Number Type . Enter a value in the input field. Read the equivalent values in the Binary, Decimal, and Hex sections. Conversion occurs as you type. To use one of the results as the next input, select the up-arrow button beside that result. Input Formats Type Valid digits Example Bit 0 and 1 101101 Decimal Decimal digits; a minus sign is supported for negative values 45 or -12 Hex 0 – 9 , A – F , or a – f 2D or a4 Whitespace is removed before conversion. An invalid value triggers a warning. When entering hexadecimal with an odd number of digits, the converter pads a leading zero internally before decoding it. Clear Values Select the top Clear button to clear the input field. Select the bottom Clear button to clear the Binary, Decimal, and Hex results.

docs.text: Type Valid digits Example Bit 0 and 1 101101 Decimal Decimal digits; a minus sign is supported for negative values 45 or -12 Hex 0 – 9 , A – F , or a – f 2D or a4 Whitespace is removed before conversion. An invalid value triggers a warning. When entering hexadecimal with an odd number of digits, the converter pads a leading zero internally before decoding it.

docs.text: OID Information Dialog Guide The OID Information dialog looks up Object Identifier (OID) details from an OID or one of its supported representations. Open it from Tool > OID Information . Figure 1. OID Information dialog. Choose an input representation and enter its value; the matching fields are populated as you type. Screen Areas Input type — Select the representation of the value to search for. Input field — Enter the value. The placeholder text changes to indicate the expected input. OID — Displays the dotted-decimal object identifier. OID Value Hex — Displays the hexadecimal encoding of the OID value. OID Hex — Displays the BER-encoded OID in hexadecimal form. Short Name — Displays the OID's short name, when available. Long Name — Displays the OID's long name, when available. Nid — Displays the numeric identifier (NID), when available. Clear — Clears the displayed result fields. Close — Closes the dialog. The lookup runs as you type or change the input type. The result fields are read-only. Supported Input Types Input type What to enter Example format OID Dotted-decimal OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1 OIDValueHex Hexadecimal OID value bytes Hexadecimal characters, for example 2A864886F70D010101 OIDHex BER-encoded OID bytes in hexadecimal Hexadecimal characters, for example 06092A864886F70D010101 ShortName OID short name For example, rsaEncryption LongName OID long name Enter the name used by the OID database. Nid Numeric identifier A numeric NID value. Look Up an OID Choose the appropriate input type from the selector. Enter or paste the corresponding value in the input field. Read the resolved OID and any available associated values below. Select Clear to clear the result fields before another lookup, or replace the input to search again. If a name or NID is not known to the OID database, some result fields may remain blank. The dialog does not provide a separate Search button; lookup is triggered by changes to the input. Notes OIDValueHex and OIDHex are different: OIDHex includes the BER tag and length bytes, while OIDValueHex contains the OID value bytes. Short name, long name, and NID are shown only when the underlying OID database has corresponding entries. The dialog also contains a Create action in the UI definition, but it is hidden by the current application implementation; it is therefore not part of the visible workflow shown above.
